question: Should OpenClaw formally standardize aggregate recovery-point handoff and restored-admission sidecars now, and if so should they be accepted as a separate/addendum RFC rather than expanding the completed SQLite artifact contract?
rationale: The proposed text establishes a durable cross-host contract and determines which lifecycle guarantees belong to OpenClaw versus external hosts; source review cannot safely choose that product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Separate and approve the lifecycle addendum
options.body: Keep RFC 0013’s completed SQLite artifact scope intact and review the sidecars as an explicitly scoped follow-on contract with named compatibility commitments.

options.title: Accept the expanded RFC 0013 scope
options.body: Merge the sidecars into RFC 0013 and explicitly treat aggregate handoff and restored admission as part of that RFC’s permanent contract.

options.title: Defer the contract
options.body: Leave the current snapshot and suspension seams in place while implementation evidence matures and a narrower core need is identified.

recommendation.title: Separate and approve the lifecycle addendum
recommendation.body: Keep RFC 0013’s completed SQLite artifact scope intact and review the sidecars as an explicitly scoped follow-on contract with named compatibility commitments.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied RFC history identifies this person’s snapshot work as the core contract that the new lifecycle boundary would extend.
